common_action: charitable monetary giving / sadaqa
source_first_adjudication_basis: Q265 presents as a best-way normative criterion encouraging people like respondent to pay more sadaqa for charitable distribution; Q266 asks whether respondent typically donates money to charity or those in need. Narrow charitable-giving action and poor/charity target align; COUNTRY !=16 restriction is preserved on norm shore.

common_action: wear hijab
source_first_adjudication_basis: Q607 item 6 states a woman should dress modestly but Islam does not require hijab; Q1010c asks whether respondent’s spouse wears hijab. The conduct actor is a concrete woman instance of the norm actor class; source routing intersection is preserved.

common_action: government address/solve first most important national problem
source_first_adjudication_basis: Q31 asks for the first most important national problem government should address; Q32, conditional on Q31, asks how likely government is to solve “the most important problem you identified.” The singular follow-up binds specifically to the first/most-important problem; solving is the expected realization of addressing it.

common_action: electoral fairness vs voting
source_first_adjudication_basis: Free and fair elections as a system-level democratic criterion is not the same action as respondent casting a vote; source establishes actor/action mismatch.

common_action: freedom of speech vs petition signing
source_first_adjudication_basis: Freedom of speech is a broad institutional liberty; signing a petition is a distinct specific civic action. Source does not identify petition-signing as the norm action.

common_action: state guarantee employment vs respondent finds job
source_first_adjudication_basis: State involvement in guaranteeing employment has state as action actor; respondent finding a better job is a different actor and action.

common_action: same-school norm vs parental school-sending objection
source_first_adjudication_basis: Q39 asks whether Black and White students should attend the same schools; Q44A asks respondent objection to sending own children to a school with a few Black children. Parent-sending/objection action and general student integration criterion are not identical.

common_action: home dinner vs neighborhood residence
source_first_adjudication_basis: Home-dinner action differs from opposite-race neighbors living close; source positively establishes different action/target.

common_action: private exclusion right vs policy vote
source_first_adjudication_basis: Norm concerns homeowners’ claimed right to racially exclude; hypothetical conduct is respondent voting on a housing law. Different actors/actions despite common housing-discrimination topic.

common_action: prioritize work over leisure vs employment status
source_first_adjudication_basis: “Work should always come first, even if it means less spare time” norm is prioritization of work over leisure; employment status does not measure that prioritization.

common_action: provide long-term care vs coresidence
source_first_adjudication_basis: Duty to provide long-term care for parents is not the same action as living with parents/parents-in-law. Source establishes different conduct.

common_action: gendered earn/home-care role vs employment status
source_first_adjudication_basis: Gender-role norm has two actor-specific clauses (man earns; woman looks after home/family). Q82 is a multi-category employment-status item; at implementation grain source does not preserve the sex-conditioned action identity needed to bind either clause without response-level reconstruction.

common_action: divorce justifiability vs divorced status
source_first_adjudication_basis: Divorce-justifiability norm and current legal marital status share a divorce concept, but source does not establish that a “divorced” status records respondent’s own divorce conduct/agency rather than an outcome involving another actor. Preserve unresolved rather than infer conduct.

common_action: help poor broadly vs donate money
source_first_adjudication_basis: Q263 says “helping the poor” at varying personal cost without specifying monetary donation; Q266 specifically measures donating money. Source proves Q263 action is broader than Q266.

common_action: woman travel alone vs irregular migration intent
source_first_adjudication_basis: Norm concerns permissibility of a woman traveling abroad by herself; Q104c concerns respondent considering leaving country without required papers and does not establish traveling alone. Target/condition/action mismatch is source-proven.

common_action: equal divorce decision rights vs marital status
source_first_adjudication_basis: Equal rights in making the decision to divorce is about decision authority; current social/marital status does not record equality of divorce decision rights.

common_action: hidden list-experiment divorce approval vs marital status
source_first_adjudication_basis: Q860A is a list experiment returning only the number of approved behaviors; it includes husband-divorce but deliberately withholds which listed behavior was approved. Item-specific norm identity cannot be bound to marital-status conduct.

common_action: tell government needs vs contact official
source_first_adjudication_basis: GB19 statement 1 says people should tell government what needs to be done; GBC17a records contacting a government official because of problems, but source does not state the content of that contact. Same-topic contact is insufficient to infer the norm action.

common_action: second-ranked problem vs singular most-important follow-up
source_first_adjudication_basis: Q32 refers singularly to “the most important problem”; Q31b is explicitly the second most important problem. Source rank wording positively excludes this cell.
